issues.description: Element: DD constructor. Problem statement (problem_statement.md) claims the DD constructor "only takes a single parameter `node: DDNode`". Both the template implementation (template_repository/dd.py) and the reference solution (solution_repository/dd.py) define DD as a dataclass with two fields: `node: DDNode` and `weight: np.complex128`, meaning the constructor requires both a node and a weight (DD(node, weight)). This discrepancy can mislead students who try to instantiate DD directly or follow the textual guidance; they may write DD(TERM) or expect a one-argument constructor and get errors or confusion about how to set edge weights. It also contradicts subsequent examples in the code and the intended use of helper constants (ONE_TERM, ZERO_TERM) and make_dd.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the problem statement to reflect the actual DD constructor signature and preferred usage. Specifically, replace or remove the sentence claiming a single-parameter constructor and state: "The DD dataclass takes two fields: node: DDNode and weight: np.complex128 (i.e., DD(node, weight)). Students should not instantiate DD/DDNode directly in most cases; instead use the provided helper functions and constants (make_dd, ONE_TERM, ZERO_TERM) to construct DDs." This preserves the pedagogical intent while matching the template and solution code.
